general: no generic Star Trek or Star Wars visual copying
no pristine showroom interiors during sustained operations
no faceless civilian masses used only as background suffering
no gibberish text as a focal element
no warped anatomy or duplicated people
aegis: never use Aegis Crown as the ship name
no fantasy shield-wall imagery substituted for actual ship systems and maneuver
no effortless rescue without visible constraints, transfer paths or resource cost
no default assumption that every crisis must be solved by firing weapons
no invulnerable hero-ship framing; damage, maintenance and redundancy must remain credible
space: no atmospheric banking like aircraft unless thrusters justify it
no weightless debris behaving like falling rain
no random decorative nebulae unless the scripted region calls for them
no scale ambiguity between Aegis Vigil, escorts, shuttles and civilian vessels
camera: no frantic camera movement that hides rescue geography
no close framing that erases the protected objective when the scene depends on spatial stakes
